paper_title: MARBLE A Hard Benchmark for Multimodal Spatial Reasoning and Planning
caption: The influence of number of blanks to .
model_annotation: The plot illustrates how model accuracy changes as the number of blanks varies for a single system labeled “Qwen2.5-VL-72B.” The x-axis is labeled “# Blanks,” uses a linear scale, and spans integer values from 1 to 6 with tick labels at every 1 blank. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy (%),” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0 up to approximately 70 (with regularly spaced tick labels at about 20-point intervals: 0, 20, 40, 60). A single light-blue solid line with circular markers shows accuracy decreasing as blanks increase: it starts near about 70% at 1 blank, drops to roughly 22% at 2 blanks, declines further to around 5% at 3 blanks, then approaches near-zero values around ~1% at 4 blanks and remains very close to 0% at 5 and 6 blanks.
